messages:
maya: Heads-up — PR #4981 (microbatching refactor) got merged to main earlier and our perf dashboard just showed a ~12% drop in throughput for mmap-backed models. Can someone take a quick look? cc @sam @kevin :eyes:

sam: assuming this is the change that switched continuous-batching->microbatch-windowing? I can run the nightly benchmark locally and post numbers in ~30m. Do we have the specific test that regressed?

kevin: I ran a quick local run against the repro script: `scripts/bench/microbatch_repro.sh --model llama-13b --seq 2048 --qps 20 --runs 5`. Seeing similar drop and a 200MB higher RSS on the worker. Paste of one run: 
```
run 3: tok/s 11200 -> baseline 12700
max_rss: 6.2G -> baseline 6.0G
p50 latency: 74ms -> baseline 68ms
```

maya: thanks. The only change in #4981 was the batching window switch + a small KV-cache touch to avoid extra memcpy. It's odd to see higher RSS. @zhen do you think this could be due to the new buffer lifetime extension?

zhen: possible — I added a short-lived ref to the prefix buffer to avoid copies during async dispatch. That could keep pages resident longer. Will try removing the ref in a i-claim patch and run the same bench.

ci-bot: CI perf job for PR #4981: nightly-bench/microbatch — status: failed (throughput decreased by 11.8%). See logs: https://ci.internal/bench/4981/summary

sam: can you post the exact bench flags you ran, kevin? also, did you observe any change in tail latency?

kevin: flags: `--microbatch-window 8 --prefetch 2 --kv-mode mmap`. Tail looked slightly worse p95 +9%. Full output gist: https://gist.github.com/kevin/mb-regress-17533

maya: ok. to triage: 1) zhen will test with the ref removed, 2) sam will rerun with baseline binary (before #4981) and compare, 3) i'll open a temporary revert PR if we confirm. Also please add a small heap profile snapshot if you can (`MALLOC_CONF=prof` style).

zhen: quick update — removed the ref in a branch `zhen/mb-ref-temp` and local bench looks back to baseline within noise (+1%). Pasted run: 
```
run 2: tok/s 12650 (baseline 12700)
max_rss: 6.0G
p95 latency: 102ms -> baseline 100ms
```

sam: I ran the baseline binary vs current main on the same machine. Baseline: avg tok/s 12740. Main (post-4981): 11250. Logs attached. Looks consistent with CI.

kevin: if removing the ref fixes it, maybe we can change approach: transfer buffer ownership via move + explicit ephemeral span instead of holding shared ref. I'll draft a tiny patch that drops the ref earlier.

maya: sounds good — can you push the patch as a PR and tag me? If it gets tests & perf green, i'll approve and merge. If not, i'll open revert.

kevin: PR up: #4994 — small change to buffer lifetime + added unit test for drop timing. PTAL.

ci-bot: Run triggered: perf/nightly for PR #4994 — queued.

sam: running quick smoke now against qa-02, will post numbers in ~15m.

deploy-bot: Note: no production rollout will occur until perf/nightly passes and oncall thumbs up.

maya: tiny note — please include the bench config in the PR description (seq len, qps, model) so we can reproduce in perf infra.

kevin: done. PR description contains `llama-13b, seq=2048, qps=20, microbatch-window=8`.

sam: results from qa-02: PR #4994 (fix) avg tok/s 12680, p95 back near baseline, mem normalized. Looks good to me.

maya: thanks all. I'll approve #4994 once CI completes and merge after the perf job is green. Great triage and quick turnaround. :tada:
